plotSections.title: Keystone Gate Mechanics
bullets: Plymouth Gawater explains that the keystones must be properly seated and calibrated by the gatehouse's Doorman before a gate can be safely activated; the mishap at Gilbrick was caused by incorrect activation/calibration.
Gerk, as the Doorman of the gatehouse and keeper of the Midgard keystone, is now responsible for helping the party safely operate the gates.

A keystone used to open a gate at the current gatehouse must remain there while the gate is open; the gate cannot simply be opened, traversed, and closed from the other side. The keystone can only be removed after the gate is shut, and tampering with a keystone while it is activating is dangerous.
Walker immediately activates the Reach gate despite Plymouth's explanation and travels through it with Elrus and Araden. He retrieves his sending stone before leaving.
Plymouth decides to accompany Walker, Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds for clues concerning Grixto and Galixtar.

plotSections.title: Gerk Experiments with the Gates
bullets: After Walker's departure, Gerk begins experimenting with his new ability as Doorman.
Gerk opens a gate into a murky, brackish body of water, causing a large rush of swamp-smelling water to blast through the opening and soak Sylan before Gerk closes it.

Gerk tries again more cautiously, opening the gate only slightly. This time steam and intense heat emerge, accompanied by the smell of sulfur and brimstone; the opening reveals a barren, arid, rocky landscape with geysers.

The gate openings are manifestations of reality rather than physical doors: turning the handle causes a door-like boundary to materialize, allowing the user to crack open reality and view or access another location.
The DM establishes that opening or closing one of these gates takes an action in combat.

plotSections.title: Plymouth Joins the Investigation
bullets: Plymouth had been investigating the remaining mosaics around the gatehouse when Walker asked him to accompany the expedition.
Plymouth consults Juten Prime before leaving, and she agrees that investigating further keystone usage and finding the Dragon Rider training grounds would be beneficial.
With Plymouth gone, the remaining party members will depend entirely on Gerk to operate the keystones and gates, giving Gerk a new practical responsibility while he learns how his abilities work.

chronologicalEvents: Walker asks Plymouth Gawater how to use his keystone to travel to The Reach; Plymouth explains that Gerk must calibrate and oversee the gate because he is the gatehouse's Doorman.
Plymouth explains that a keystone must remain seated in the gatehouse while its gate is open and warns that improperly handling an activating keystone can cause malfunctions.
Walker activates the gate to The Reach and leaves with Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds.
Walker returns briefly to retrieve his sending stone before departing through the gate.
Plymouth agrees to accompany Walker after consulting Juten Prime and leaves with the expedition.
Gerk experiments with his Doorman abilities by opening a portal into brackish water, accidentally blasting Sylan with water before closing it.
Gerk opens another gate cautiously and discovers a hot, sulfurous, barren landscape containing geysers.
The party learns that opening and closing a gate takes an action in combat and discusses the potential tactical uses and dangers of Gerk's new ability.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, party ambassador; keeper of the Midgard keystone and the gatehouse's Doorman.
notes: As Doorman, Gerk is responsible for calibrating and properly seating keystones before the gates can be safely activated.
Gerk begins experimenting with his new gate-opening ability and successfully opens multiple portals to unknown environments.
His first attempt releases a large quantity of brackish swamp water; his second reveals a hot, sulfurous wasteland with geysers.
With Plymouth leaving the gatehouse, Gerk becomes the sole remaining party member responsible for helping operate the keystones.
titles: Overseer of the gates at the gatehouse
personality: Eager to experiment with his newfound ability despite not yet understanding how it works.
quotesThemes: Gerk is still trying to understand what it means to be the Doorman and how to control the gates safely.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; travels with Glimmen.
notes: Uses his keystone to open the gate to The Reach and departs with Elrus and Araden.
His immediate goal is to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds for clues related to Grixto and Galixtar.
Retrieves his sending stone before leaving the gatehouse.
Plymouth joins Walker's expedition.
personality: Impatient and confident about using the keystone, activating the gate immediately after receiving Plymouth's explanation.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer investigating the gatehouse mosaics and keystones.
notes: Has a general understanding of how the keystones and gates operate.
Explains that keystones must be calibrated and seated correctly by the gatehouse's Doorman to prevent malfunctions.
Consults Juten Prime before leaving the gatehouse and receives approval to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds.
Equips himself for travel with a leather backpack, traveling cloak, short sword, and additional pouches before joining Walker's expedition.
Leaves the gatehouse with Walker, Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds.
personality: Methodical and investigative, but willing to accompany the party when the investigation could provide useful information about the keystones or Dragon Riders.
quotesThemes: Further investigation into keystone usage and the Dragon Rider training grounds could provide valuable information.

Juten Prime.existing: Known NPC associated with the party's current base of operations.
notes: Approves Plymouth accompanying Walker's expedition because investigating keystone usage and locating the Dragon Rider training grounds could be beneficial.
Keystones must be properly oriented, calibrated, and seated in the gatehouse before activation.
The Doorman is responsible for helping calibrate the keystones and prevent gate malfunctions.
A keystone remains at the originating gatehouse while its gate is open.
Removing or tampering with an activating keystone is dangerous.
The gates can be opened by manipulating a door-like interface that materializes as a manifestation of the surrounding reality rather than a permanent physical door.
Opening a gate can expose the gatehouse to environmental hazards from the destination, such as water, steam, heat, or other substances.
Opening and closing a gate takes an action in combat.
A gate opened from a gatehouse is effectively one-way until it is closed from the originating side.
The expedition is traveling there to investigate clues connected to Grixto and Galixtar.
The grounds were associated with the Dragon Rider guild that Elrus and Araden belonged to.
Walker remembers to retrieve his sending stone from the gatehouse before departing for The Reach.

misTranscriptions.notes: Appears alongside Galixtar in the context of investigating where they are hiding.
Appears alongside Grixto in the context of investigating their hiding place.
No correction needed; included only as a potential ASR uncertainty because the transcript contains several distorted references around this name.

newTerms.name: Doorman
notes: The title and role given to Gerk as overseer of the gates at his chosen gatehouse.
The Doorman is responsible for calibrating and properly seating keystones so gates activate safely.

newTerms.name: Keystone Calibration
notes: Keystones must be correctly oriented and seated in a gatehouse before activation; improper calibration can cause gate malfunctions.

newTerms.name: Dragon Rider Training Grounds
notes: Training grounds associated with the Dragon Rider guild that Elrus and Araden previously belonged to; Walker's expedition is investigating them for clues about Grixto and Galixtar.
